title: Sunday Investment Thesis
summary: Fundamentals remain strong across the group, while valuation is now the main differentiator. The semiconductor names continue to show evidence of AI, HBM and advanced-packaging investment. EXE offers the most attractive current entry, while KLAC is the semiconductor name closest to its buy zone.

stocks.headline: Thesis intact; operating momentum remains excellent.
stocks.body: The latest quarter substantially validates the thesis. June-quarter revenue reached $6.72B, up 15.1% sequentially, non-GAAP gross margin reached 52%, and EPS was $1.82. September-quarter guidance increased to $8.1B ± $400M and $2.15 ± $0.15 EPS. Lam's exposure to etch and deposition, advanced memory structures and increasingly complex AI/HBM manufacturing remains exactly where we want it. At $314, however, the fundamental improvement does not warrant chasing the stock above our $285 entry. The main risks remain elevated semiconductor-equipment expectations, China exposure, export controls and eventual normalization of the memory/WFE investment cycle.
stocks.risk: Valuation, China exposure and WFE cycle normalization

stocks.headline: Record results confirm the thesis, but valuation still demands patience.
stocks.body: Applied Materials reported record $9.12B quarterly revenue, up 25% year over year, with record non-GAAP EPS of $3.50. Management's Q4 outlook is approximately $10.25B revenue and $4.02 adjusted EPS. Especially important to our thesis, AMAT now expects advanced-packaging revenue to grow more than 70% in 2026 and says customer visibility is extending toward 2030. That is excellent fundamental confirmation. The problem remains price: even after the correction to $492.32, the shares remain above our $450 entry. Expectations became extremely elevated after the semiconductor-equipment rally, which is why strong execution alone is not enough to justify chasing the stock.
stocks.catalyst: Advanced packaging growth and long customer visibility

stocks.headline: The thesis has strengthened and the valuation is becoming much more interesting.
stocks.body: KLA reported $3.66B quarterly revenue above the guidance midpoint and guided the September quarter to $4.0B ± $200M with approximately 62.5% non-GAAP gross margin. Management explicitly says AI infrastructure is increasing process-control demand in leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging, with momentum accelerating through the second half of 2026 and into 2027. That is almost a textbook confirmation of our KLA thesis. The stock has simultaneously fallen sharply from its June high. I would preserve the $170 entry rather than chase it upward. At $170 with this guidance intact, I would want to buy.
stocks.catalyst: AI-driven process-control intensity across logic, memory and packaging

stocks.headline: The highest-quality monopoly-like asset in the group remains fundamentally strong.
stocks.body: ASML's latest quarter reinforced the long-term thesis. Sales reached €9.33B, net income €2.92B and gross margin 54%, while management raised 2026 revenue guidance to €43–45B. AI adoption remains a major semiconductor-industry driver, increasing critical lithography exposures in advanced logic and memory, and High-NA EUV continues to advance toward production readiness. The ADR has corrected meaningfully from its peak, but at $1,763.76 it is still not cheap enough to move our entry. The core competitive thesis remains intact.
stocks.catalyst: EUV/High-NA intensity as AI chips become more complex

stocks.headline: Operational performance is exceptional, but the stock remains valuation-sensitive.
stocks.body: Astera Labs produced one of the strongest operating updates in the group. Revenue reached a record $392.4M, up 27% sequentially and 104% year over year, with 73.7% non-GAAP gross margin. Management expects Q3 revenue of $540–560M, roughly another 40% sequential increase at midpoint, as Scorpio switches become the company's largest product family one quarter earlier than expected. This materially strengthens the AI-fabric and connectivity thesis. Astera is broadening from retimers into a rack-scale AI connectivity platform, but customer concentration, hyperscaler spending cycles and Scorpio execution make valuation discipline important.
stocks.catalyst: Scorpio scale-up and broader rack-scale AI connectivity
stocks.risk: Customer concentration and execution at a premium multiple

stocks.headline: The best current valuation/risk-reward setup in the group.
stocks.body: Expand Energy remains my favorite current entry. The company produced 7.48 Bcfe/day, reaffirmed 2026 production of 7.4–7.6 Bcfe/day, generated $1.096B operating cash flow and reduced total debt by roughly $1.3B from year-end. Net debt is about $3.1B and leverage approximately 0.5×. The Twin Eagle acquisition expands EXE into gas marketing and logistics, giving it better positioning to connect production directly with LNG, utilities and eventually data-center and power demand. Near-term natural-gas pricing remains the key counterargument, but at $96.09 the stock is already inside our buy zone.
stocks.catalyst: LNG, power/data-center demand and Twin Eagle integration

stocks.headline: The HBM and semiconductor-test thesis has strengthened considerably.
stocks.body: Teradyne's latest results strongly validate the reason we added it. Quarterly revenue hit a record $1.329B, up 104% year over year, including $1.122B of Semiconductor Test revenue. Memory revenue exceeded $200M for the third consecutive quarter, driven by HBM/DRAM plus renewed NAND final-test demand, while Semiconductor Test revenue grew 128% year over year. Q3 guidance remains strong and management says AI demand is robust. The only thing preventing a buy is valuation: at $375.74, the shares still command a substantial multiple for a historically cyclical test-equipment business.
stocks.catalyst: HBM/DRAM and AI-driven semiconductor test demand
stocks.risk: High multiple in a historically cyclical business
